clue.text: Recovering from climbing …

definitions.meaning: to recuperate after an illness or a setback
clambering across the top of a wall or obstacle

explanation.surface: Someone is recuperating after a mountain ascent, and the sentence runs on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 7 Across for the surface only; each clue is solved on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean the same idiom: recuperating after an illness, and literally clambering across something.

clue.text: Supplied transport run within town in Kent

indicators.note: inside, so the run letter goes into the word for supplied

parts.note: gave means supplied
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
to send someone into raptures is to transport them

explanation.surface: Buses are laid on for a route through a Kentish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Gravesend is a town on the Thames estuary in Kent, south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravesend is a port town in north Kent on the south bank of the Thames.

clue.text: With seaside pollution sorted, it's safe to proceed

definitions.meaning: a whimsical literal reading: the beaches have been cleaned up
the idiom meaning nobody is watching, so go ahead

explanation.surface: Once the beach is cleaned up, people may go ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from smugglers watching the shore, means no danger is in sight; literally the shoreline is unpolluted.

clue.text: List is overseen by couple at start of engagement

indicators.note: in a down clue the couple sits above, before the word is

parts.note: a romantic couple is called an item

indicators.note: the opening letter of engagement

explanation.surface: A list of tasks is checked by a newly engaged pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to set out in a list, point by point.

clue.text: Cautious in the style of Fred's partner?

parts.note: Ginger Rogers danced with Fred Astaire
the suffix -ly turns a word into one meaning in that manner

explanation.surface: Someone dances carefully like Fred Astaire's famous co-star.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something carefully and warily, with great delicacy.

clue.text: Very long time needed to cover one's face

indicators.note: surround, so the letters for very and long time go round I'S

parts.note: an age is a very long time
one's read as one is: I (one) plus S ('s)

explanation.surface: Making up takes ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' puts the possessive phrase inside; the page printed 'on', a scanning loss of the apostrophe phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Visage is a literary word for a person's countenance.

clue.text: Unusual combination of British and Italian snack food

parts.note: rare means unusual

explanation.surface: A cross-cultural snack mixes British and Italian ingredients oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit, Welsh rabbit, is melted cheese on toast, a light snack dish.

clue.text: … peaks of very arduous range in part of France

indicators.note: the tops of words, read down the page, are their opening letters

explanation.surface: The climb continues: the summits of a tough mountain chain somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Var is a département in Provence, on the Mediterranean coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Var is a département, an administrative region, of south-eastern France.

clue.text: All I crave-a mince pie and cold topping

indicators.note: printer's pie is jumbled type, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a mince pie with a scoop of something cold on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pie' as a noun means a jumble, as in printer's pie.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoop of plain frozen dessert served on top of a pudding.

clue.text: Children's writer: Bloom by name

parts.note: a rose is a bloom or flower

explanation.surface: A children's author called Bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Rosen is a British children's poet and author, former Children's Laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Rosen wrote We're Going on a Bear Hunt and other books for young readers.

clue.text: A note written by editor for singer

parts.note: dele is the proofreader's or editor's mark telling the printer to delete something

explanation.surface: An editor jots down a memo about a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: DELE (Latin for 'delete') is the mark an editor writes in the margin to cut text.
explanation.definitionFit: Adele is a British pop vocalist, a multiple Grammy winner.

clue.text: Nine gross assorted decorative items

indicators.note: mixed up, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone orders nine gross of various ornaments.
explanation.definitionFit: Rings worn through the nostril are ornaments, pieces of facial jewellery.

clue.text: Inspiring feelings about book I have to finish

indicators.note: the contracted I have comes last, at the end of the word
turned about, so the word for a book is read backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large book
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A reader says a stirring volume is something they must get to the end of.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that stirs up emotion, as an emotive speech arouses strong reactions.

clue.text: Ignoble, spoiling tapestry

indicators.note: ruining the word, so its letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A dishonourable act ruins a woven wall hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: Gobelin tapestries come from the famous Paris works of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobelin is a type of richly woven wall hanging from the Paris manufactory.

clue.text: Wind blowing later? Yes

indicators.note: blown about, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Asked whether a gale will get up later, someone agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind coming from the east is named after its direction, as a noun.

clue.text: Old engineer retires to a city in Canada

indicators.note: goes back, so the engineer's name is read in reverse

parts.note: James Watt, the Scottish engineer of steam-engine fame

explanation.surface: An elderly engineer moves to a Canadian city for his retirement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the federal capital of Canada, in Ontario.

clue.text: Skill shown by a department head

parts.note: a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Competence displayed by the boss of a department.
explanation.definitionFit: Adeptness is proficiency, being expert at something.

clue.text: He's getting his act together as airline entrepreneur, touring extremely warm area

indicators.note: travelling round, so the entrepreneur's name encloses the other letters

parts.note: Freddie Laker founded Laker Airways

indicators.note: the very ends, first and last letters, of warm

explanation.surface: An airline magnate visits a hot region while trying to sort himself out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'act' is a parliamentary Act: a legislator puts acts together. Sir Freddie Laker ran a cut-price British airline.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislator drafts and passes Acts, statutes, so literally puts his Act together.

clue.text: Crossing river cuckoo gets a bit wet

indicators.note: going across, so the word for cuckoo straddles the river letter

parts.note: dippy and cuckoo both mean crazy

explanation.surface: Someone wading across a stream, being daft, gets splashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet in the British sense of feeble or soppy; drippy means insipid and sentimental.

clue.text: Sounds like cool performer in Cats, musical's principal character

indicators.note: the signal that the answer matches spoken words

parts.note: to fan is to cool, and a tom is a male cat, a performer in the show Cats

explanation.surface: A stylish actor in Cats is the star of a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: The Phantom is the title role of Lloyd Webber's The Phantom of the Opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The masked figure is the title role of Lloyd Webber's Opera musical.

clue.text: Penny's perhaps a very tiny amount

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny in British money
the word a is one example of an article in grammar, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: A penny might be thought of as a minuscule sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is the indefinite article; 'perhaps' warns that it is one example. The 's after Penny is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A speck or atom of something, the smallest possible quantity.

clue.text: Tense about working this evening

indicators.note: around, so the word for tense surrounds the word for working

parts.note: tight means taut or tense
on means working or operating

explanation.surface: Someone nervous about a work shift later today.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight refers to the coming evening or night of today.

clue.text: Jog on motorway, getting in difficulty for a start

parts.note: re means on or concerning
M designates a motorway in Britain, as in the M1
the word in, taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of difficulty is used

explanation.surface: A jogger on a motorway is soon in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone's memory is to prompt them about something.

clue.text: State department leaders left beset by bother

parts.note: the leading two letters of the word department

indicators.note: surrounded by, so the letter for left sits inside the word for bother

parts.note: to care is to bother, to trouble oneself

explanation.surface: Heads of a government ministry, besieged by trouble, issue a statement.
explanation.definitionFit: To state is to announce or assert something formally, a verb.

clue.text: Daughter attends booze-up in warehouse

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily

explanation.surface: A daughter goes to a drinking party at a storage building.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a storehouse or storage building.

clue.text: Chap at ninety has little time to keep a pet

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: holding on to, so the letters for ninety and time surround the a

parts.note: XC is ninety in Roman numerals
t is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A ninety-year-old man has only a short while left to look after a companion animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Manx cat is the tailless breed from the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailless breed of domestic feline kept as a companion animal.

clue.text: Relax with wife in choice Scottish town

indicators.note: placed inside, so rest plus the wife letter go within the word for choice

parts.note: the pick of something is the choice
to rest is to relax

explanation.surface: A couple take a holiday in a favourite Scottish resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestwick is a town on the Ayrshire coast of Scotland, known for its airport and golf.

clue.text: Clergyman's property some rebel grabbed in revolution

indicators.note: turned round, so the letters taken are read backwards
only part of the words rebel grabbed is taken

explanation.surface: A rebel seizes a vicar's estate during an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Glebe land is the parcel of land attached to a parish benefice, owned by the incumbent.

clue.text: Uttered word of appreciation for sailor

indicators.note: spoken, so the word is matched by how it is said

parts.note: ta is British slang for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone said thanks to a seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar (or Jack Tar) is an old slang name for a seaman.

clue.text: Mimer doesn't act badly in silent movie

indicators.note: performing poorly, so the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A performer of mime keeps quiet but does not perform poorly in a film without sound.
explanation.walkthrough: Modern Times (1936) is Charlie Chaplin's last largely silent film.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin's 1936 film was made almost wholly without dialogue.
